claims.text: The index cache in ``index.py`` is in-memory
every server restart re-pays the full scan

claims.text: We read every file's bytes anyway, so hashing is nearly free
claims.why: File reading not shown in this chunk.

claims.why: Depends on file_key being used with content hash; not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: A stale cache silently reporting wrong code health would be worse than a slow scan, so the key is chosen so staleness is not representable.
claims.why: Requires full cache logic to verify.

claims.text: Failure policy: this is an optimization, never a correctness dependency. Any sqlite problem degrades to "no cache" and the build proceeds normally.
claims.why: Sqlite handling not in this chunk.

claims.why: _decode and deletion logic not in this chunk.

claims.why: Function checks DAEDALUS_CACHE_DIR first, returns that path.

claims.text: Digest of the extractor's own source, folded into every key.
claims.why: Function hashes parse.py and returns hex digest.

claims.text: ``ANALYSIS_VERSION`` is hand-maintained, so it only invalidates the cache if someone remembers to bump it.
claims.why: ANALYSIS_VERSION not defined in this chunk.
Depends on behavior of file_key using _parser_version.

claims.text: Unreadable source degrades to the manual constant alone (never break the build for an optimization).
claims.why: Exception handler returns empty string, which is included in key; build not broken.

claims.text: Content-addressed key. ``rel`` is included because analysis embeds the module path (CodeUnit.module), so the same bytes at two paths are two different results.

tiktoken is optional and installing/removing it changes no source byte, so without this segment every file is a cache HIT across that change: the cached n_tokens (old tokenizer) sums into total_tokens (the distill denominator) while the slice numerator is recounted under the NEW tokenizer -- a silent mixed-tokenizer ratio that slice.py still stamps whole_repo_tokens_exact=True. Keying on tokenizer identity turns that into a miss (recompute under the current tokenizer) instead.
claims.why: tokenizer_name() not defined in this chunk; behavior of slice.py not visible.

claims.text: JSON, not pickle: the cache file is on disk and pickle would make a tampered cache an arbitrary-code-execution vector.
claims.why: Serialization code not fully present; only _enc_type shown.

claims.text: Encoded as nested plain LISTS, positionally, in declaration-field order -- exactly the style ``units`` uses for ``CodeUnit``.

Written out by hand rather than via ``dataclasses.astuple``/``asdict`` for two reasons: a reflective codec would silently start round-tripping a NEW field the moment one is added to ``parse.py`` (so the cache would carry a field this generation of the decoder does not know how to place), and it would hide the one thing that actually needs care below -- JSON has no tuple, so every ``tuple[str, ...]`` field must be RE-TUPLED on the way in. A list where extraction produced a tuple changes ``repr`` and dataclass equality, which is enough to break the byte-identity assertions the type layer is held to (a cache HIT would not equal a cache MISS).
claims.why: Decoder and equality checks not in this chunk.

observations.what: file_key does not include language parameter despite docstring claim.
cache_root does not validate or create the directory.
_enc_type is incomplete due to truncation; may be missing fields.
Non-UTF-8 characters in rel, spec_name, text are replaced with replacement character, potentially causing collisions or data loss.
enabled() checks only '1' and 'true' case-insensitively; other truthy values like 'yes' not considered.
_parser_version uses lru_cache with maxsize=1, but the function takes no arguments; caching is redundant but harmless.
